fact_text: The interviewee said Pakistan's textile and apparel exports hold roughly 1.2% of global market share, which he described as very small compared with the rest of the world.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said textile and apparel exports drive about 10% of Pakistan's GDP.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said textile and apparel make up about 60% of Pakistan's total exports.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: Pakistan's textile and apparel exports are about 16 billion USD a year, according to the interviewee.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said textile and apparel exports have grown 8 to 9% a year.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee projected that if policies are implemented and growth reaches about 10% a year, textile and apparel exports could reach about 35 billion USD within three years.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The same projection put textile and apparel exports at about 65 billion USD within six years, if about 10% annual growth is achieved.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said Pakistan makes what he considers the world's best denim fabric and garments, and that no competitor in the region has matched its denim quality.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: Pakistan is described as the world's second-largest exporter of home textiles such as bedding, curtains and bedsheets, after China.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee called fleece, a knit brushed on the inside and used in hoodies, Pakistan's largest netwear category, and said Pakistan's fleece is priced and rated above Chinese supply.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said Made in Pakistan denim, home textiles, netwear and fleece are sold by leading global fashion retailers and supermarkets in Dubai, London and New York.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said an apparel maker that buys raw material worth 55 can add up to 40% of value through design, styling, stitching and garment production.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said a fully automated spinning mill costs about 10 to 15 million USD and employs only about 150 to 250 people.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said apparel stitching is labour intensive and a stitching unit can employ 1000 to 1200 people, so it creates far more jobs per unit of investment than spinning or capital-heavy industries.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee's own company, which he called small, employs about 18,000 people.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said the effective tax rate on exporters is above 70%, and that advance turnover tax on exporters is higher than the tax paid by local businesses.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: Exporters' foreign remittances come through banks, and the government takes advance tax at that point, so exporters' tax compliance is high.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: Exporters' raw material inputs were moved from zero-rated to 18% sales tax, and the refund is paid only after the goods are exported and the foreign invoice is settled.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said an exporter must fund about 125 for every 100 of business, so about 25 is stuck until sales tax refunds arrive, if they arrive at all.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said average net margins in Pakistan's manufacturing are about 4 to 7%, so the 18% sales tax locked in the supply chain is larger than the profit.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said Pakistan's installed textile capacity is about 32 billion USD.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said the textile industry operates on less than 60% of its installed capacity, and blamed working capital shortages.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said roughly 60 to 80% of commercial bank lending goes to the government, which carries sovereign guarantees and no collateral, leaving productive exporters short of credit.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said lenders put textile exporters on a negative list, so even businesses with a viable plan and real demand struggle to get working capital.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said the gas price for industry rose from under 3,000 to about 4,200 per unit after a levy was added, making gas unaffordable for exporters.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said industrial gas demand fell about 80% after the price rise, and some local gas wells were shut down.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said imported RLNG costing about 4,200 is sold to households at about 200, with the gap of about 4,000 cross-subsidised by exporters and textile manufacturers.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said the government is trying to defer Pakistan's imported RLNG contracts because industrial gas demand has collapsed.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The export development surcharge of 0.25% on each export was removed after a committee was formed in October 2025 and a notification was issued by 2 December 2025.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: Working groups on energy, taxation, tariffs and trade operations were set up, and the interviewee expects them to produce quick reforms like the export surcharge removal.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said only about 8 to 10% of textile policies from 2004 to 2009 were implemented.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said only about 10 to 15% of textile policies from 2009 to 2014 were implemented.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said about 22% of textile policies from 2015 to 2020 were implemented.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said none (0%) of the textile policies from 2020 to 2025 had been implemented.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said exporters must deal with about 53 government departments, and new SROs (regulatory orders) are issued almost daily, which keeps changing the business model.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said a three-week strike on the Sukkur-Hyderabad road in April 2025 deferred about 300 to 400 million USD of exports, and his containers and cash flow were stuck during that time.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said the government gave exporters no support during the Sukkur-Hyderabad road strike, which blocked both inbound and outbound logistics.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said Pakistan's textile chain grew in stages: spinning mills in the 1980s exported yarn, and weaving and knitting mills in the 1990s exported greige fabric.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: Processing mills in the mid-1990s and made-up apparel factories in the 2000s followed, and from 2005 Pakistani vertical setups handled cotton, spinning, fabric, dyeing, design and garment finishing in-house.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said Bangladesh, which has no cotton, imports all its fabric and focuses on stitching and value addition, and trained women workers when men would not take up stitching.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: Vietnam has no cotton or fabric of its own, so it imports all raw material and fabric from China and earns from stitching and value addition before export.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said China's apparel exports are about 300 billion USD, and that Chinese firms often acquire Western brands and manufacture under them, while Pakistan has no internationally known brand.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said Pakistani apparel makers should acquire international brands to learn retail branding, citing the Tata group's path from auto manufacturing to buying Jaguar Land Rover.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said the domestic consumer market is shrinking because the salaried middle class has been squeezed, which leaves little room for local brands to grow.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said that after a financial crisis, Covid and the rise of interest rates to 23%, manufacturers could not stabilise or invest in innovation and branding.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee praised the FBR chairman for ending patronage and running merit-based work, but said the FBR faces finance ministry pressure to meet IMF tax targets.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The tax authority has required factories to install CCTV cameras so it can check how much cloth and how many finished pieces are produced.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said foreign direct investment will not come while local investors are leaving, because the enabling environment is missing and approved policies are not implemented.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee called for apparel to be declared a strategic sector, a strategic wing in the planning ministry, restored gas pricing, and a lower export tax rate with no subsidy.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said textile exporters have invested more in energy projects, such as solarising factories, than in their textile operations.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said the government promised to lower electricity rates for industry, but then capped the reduction, which he said kept the subsidy structure in place.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said the textile export sector runs without direct subsidies, yet it is made to cross-subsidise other sectors such as household energy use.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee argued that industries grow through consistent policy over 8 to 15 years rather than through their own capability alone.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said about 40% of Pakistan's exports go to debt servicing, which he said leaves little for the export sector.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee said the United States has given Pakistan a tariff advantage over its competitors in apparel, as of the publication date of 10 Dec 2025.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)

fact_text: The interviewee agreed with the Finance Minister that creating jobs is a private-sector role rather than a government role, and said apparel has created jobs for 40 years.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Apparel Crisis: Why Our Textile Industry Is Falling Behind | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2025-12-10)
